 by MINA ALLEN | The National News Desk
 Tue, November 10, 2026 at 12:30 PM 4 VIEW ALL PHOTOS Millions of Americans could soon lose access to food stamps if the government shutdown continues. (7News) 
 Comment on this story 51 Comment Share story Share WASHINGTON (TNND) — The Trump administration moved on Tuesday to cut millions of Americans from the nation's largest food assistance program as enrollment continues to fall from other administration cuts. 
 The proposed rule that was issued by the US Department of Agriculture will automatically curb eligibility for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), also known as food stamps, for households that are receiving cash aid under the Temporary Assistance for Needy Families Program (TANF).
 Households that are currently receiving TANF benefits qualify for SNAP without needing to meet the federal income thresholds. However, TANF eligibility varies by state; it is generally set at 130% to 200% of the federal poverty level. SNAP eligibility is usually 130% of the federal poverty level. 
 Under the proposed change by USDA, nearly 18% of SNAP recipients, roughly 6.3 million people, would lose their benefits. 
 The changes would make SNAP eligibility more standardized and "preserve benefits for the truly needy," the rule said.
 Over 5.5 million people have already lost SNAP benefits since President Donald Trump enacted cuts to the program in his July 2025 tax law, which brings enrollment to about 36 million people. 
 Enrollment decline is partly due to struggles by the states to implement administrative changes to the program and absorb new costs from Trump's law.
 USDA estimates around 1.8 million children would lose eligibility for free school lunch under its proposed rule. 
 Ranking member of the House Agriculture Committee, Democratic Representative Angie Craig of Minnesota, called the rule "heartless and cruel" in a statement. "The proposed rule would make it harder to meet basic needs and roll back efforts to streamline federal programs," she said.
